claims.subject: turbopump assembly specific horsepower
claims.object: 2.22 hp/lbm (Redstone) to above 10 (Saturn V F-1, J-2) in about 10 years; SSME expected above 100
claims.statement: NASA SP-8107 reports turbopump assembly specific horsepower rising from 2.22 hp/lbm for the Redstone to values above 10 for the Saturn V (F-1 and J-2) in about ten years, with SSME turbopumps expected to exceed 100; turbopumps have the highest power-to-weight ratio in rotating machinery.
qualifiers: turbine-driven turbopump assemblies; not electric pumps
claims.quote: 2.22 for the Redstone turbopump assembly to values greater than 10 for the Saturn V

claims.subject: SP-8107 Table I turbopump data
claims.object: best available data as of mid-1973 for operational turbopump systems; SSME not operational, at emergency power level
claims.statement: SP-8107 Table I values are the best available data as of mid-1973 for operational turbopump systems; the SSME entry is not operational, presented for comparison, at emergency power level.
claims.quote: Numbers presented are those for a turbopump operational system

empirical_constants.name: A-7 (Redstone) turbopump assembly specific horsepower
empirical_constants.context: Table I: efficiency 26.4%, weight 332 lbm; TURBOPUMP ASSEMBLY specific horsepower (assembly power per assembly weight; turbine-driven), mid-1973 data; not an electric pump or motor value; 1 hp/lbm = 1.644 kW/kg (reviewer unit conversion) -> 3.65 kW/kg
